subject: Help: Time data from Java in Renjin

messages.author: f7918128c15e26ee
messages.subject: Help: Time data from Java in Renjin
parts:
Hi !

I am using Renjin to merger an R calculation in Java project.

I almost succeed except the time data from Java. The time data type is like:    parseDateString("2015-02-25T13:02:22Z")
Originally, I could use     strptime(TimeDataName, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")   to read those data as time series in R, but now it does not work and result in data type as "externalptr" .

Because those time data from Java has other important use, therefore may not be changed to other type like string in Java.

Could anyone please help me figure this out? Many thanks!!!

messages.author: da2d889d1cc5c83c
messages.subject: Re: Help: Time data from Java in Renjin
parts:
Hi Charles,

I don´t know if your problem is the same as Anton´s, but I realized that in Anton´s case where he was parsing a csv file with dates in it, the dates did not come out correctly.  I have the impression that Renjin is assuming that anything that starts with a number is a number.  So, in Anton´s case, only 2015 was converted from the date.  I suggested (and I don´t know if this is possible) trying to change the date to another format, for instance, feb/25/2015T13:02:22Z, so that Renjin seens it is a string and not a number. 

Yet, your case might be completely different.  Hope this helps... if I does, let me know.


Thanks

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Help: Time data from Java in Renjin
parts:
Hi Charles,
It looks like orderOpenTime is a Java object? The error message is basically saying: "I don't know how to divide a Java object (externalptr) by a double-precision floating point number".

java.util.Date has a getTime() method which returns the time as the number of milliseconds since the epoch:

trades[[2]]$orderOpenTime$time

should invoke this method and return a normal R number value

So your expression should be:

 as.POSIXct(trades[[2]]$orderOpenTime$time/1000, origin="1970-01-01")

HTH,
Alex

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Help: Time data from Java in Renjin
parts:
Right, so if you were in Java land, you would write:

long timeInMillis = trades.get(2).getOrderOpenTime().getTime()

which gives you a unix timestamp: the number of milliseconds since Jan 1 1970

Renjin understands 'long' values, it doesn't (currently) understand anything specific about java.util.Date objects, other than the fact that's a java object with properties. 

So you can write in R:

timeInMillis <- trades[[2]]$orderOpenTime$time

This in turn is value you can convert to an R date object using the expression

 as.POSIXct(timeInMillis/1000, origin="1970-01-01")

Does that make sense?

Best,
Alex
